newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Base metals surge higher led by copper.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Base metals surge higher led by copper.

text.p: Investors piled into the copper market on Thursday which instilled confidence throughout the base metals sector.
Elsewhere in commodity markets sterling's fall saw London cocoa futures close higher while weather considerations sent corn and soyabean prices tumbling.

The London Metal Exchange (LME) three months delivery copper futures moved above $2,300 a tonne which trigggered a wave of buying interest from speculators but not too much confidence that it could be sustained.

"I can't find any fundamental reason for the move," said James Steel, metals analyst with Refco Inc. "The funds are getting into the act to a limited degree. But fundamentally the market looks weak," he said.
The price reached $2,335 a tonne, up $37 from Wednesday, before profittaking moved in.

A solid rise in the LME's flagship contract usually encourages players in other metals and zinc and aluminium both attracted buying interest which resulted in gains of $12 and $21 a tonne respectively.
These two metals were also aided by squeezes in supplies available to the market over the next few weeks, which is prompting unusually high premiums to be paid for nearby delivery metal.
I was to this end that LME chief-executive David King in a notice reminded members of rules regarding market conditions and abuse.
"Circumstances may vary, but a member could have a long position which is large in relation to the stock available for delivery," the notice said.
"When assessing such issues, the LME Board or disciplinary committee may judge the effect on market conditions, whether or not the parties involved intended to create such conditions." it said.
While saying that the notice was for guidance, the LME said "In the event of a breach of the LME rules, the LME will not hesitate to take disciplinary proceedings against members."

On the cocoa market some trade buying coupled with the effect of sterling's fall agains the dollar saw London market cocoa prices show gains of around 10 sterling a tonne despite a fall in the New York market.

In Chicago weather-watching traders knocked corn and soyabean prices down further as private U.S. forecaster said there was a slight chance of heavier rains in the Midwest growing areas over the week-end.
Corn was down around five cents a bushel at $2.53 and soyabeans dropped up around 13 cents to $6.66 a bushel.
